translations.literal: The Master of Horse ascends by the west steps, before the west pillar, faces south, waves the bow, and orders the marker-holder with the banner to leave the target ten paces west, north to the exhaustion marker and stop.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Horse ascends by the west steps, before the west pillar, faces south, waves the bow, and orders the marker-holder with the banner to leave the target ten paces west, north to the exhaustion marker and stop.

sentences.zh: 司馬降自西階，復位。

translations.literal: The Master of Horse descends by the west steps and returns to his place.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Horse descends by the west steps and returns to his place.

sentences.zh: 千牛中郎一人奉決、拾以笥，千牛將軍奉弓，千牛郎將奉矢，進，立於御榻東少南，西向。

translations.literal: One Imperial Ox middle attendant bears thumb-ring and armguard in the quiver; the Imperial Ox general bears the bow; the Imperial Ox lieutenant bears arrows; they advance and stand east of the imperial couch slightly south, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: One Imperial Ox middle attendant bears thumb-ring and armguard in the quiver; the Imperial Ox general bears the bow; the Imperial Ox lieutenant bears arrows; they advance and stand east of the imperial couch slightly south, facing west.

sentences.zh: 郎將跪奠笥於御榻前，少東。

translations.literal: The commandant kneels and places the quiver before the couch, slightly east.
translations.idiomatic: The commandant kneels and places the quiver before the couch, slightly east.

sentences.zh: 遂拂以巾，取決，興。

translations.literal: He then brushes with a cloth, takes the thumb-ring, and rises.
translations.idiomatic: He then brushes with a cloth, takes the thumb-ring, and rises.

sentences.zh: 贊設決。

translations.literal: The announcer says: "Set the thumb-ring."
translations.idiomatic: The announcer says: "Set the thumb-ring."

sentences.zh: 又跪取拾，興，贊設拾。

translations.literal: Again kneeling he takes the armguard, rises; the announcer says: "Set the armguard."
translations.idiomatic: Again kneeling he takes the armguard, rises; the announcer says: "Set the armguard."

sentences.zh: 以笥退，奠於坫。

translations.literal: He withdraws with the quiver and places it on the altar.
translations.idiomatic: He withdraws with the quiver and places it on the altar.

sentences.zh: 千牛將軍北面張弓，以袂順左右隈，上再下一，弓左右隈，謂弓面上下。

translations.literal: The Imperial Ox general faces north and draws the bow, running the sleeve along left and right nooks—upper twice, lower once; left and right nooks of the bow mean the upper and lower faces of the bow.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Ox general faces north and draws the bow, running the sleeve along left and right nooks—upper twice, lower once; left and right nooks of the bow mean the upper and lower faces of the bow.

sentences.zh: 以衣袂摩拭上面再，下面一。

translations.literal: He wipes the upper face twice and the lower once with the sleeve.
translations.idiomatic: He wipes the upper face twice and the lower once with the sleeve.

sentences.zh: 西面，左執弣、右執簫以進。

translations.literal: Facing west, left hand on the grip, right hand on the bow tip, he advances.
translations.idiomatic: Facing west, left hand on the grip, right hand on the bow tip, he advances.

sentences.zh: 千牛郎將以巾拂矢進，一一供御。

translations.literal: The Imperial Ox lieutenant brushes arrows with a cloth and advances them one by one for the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Ox lieutenant brushes arrows with a cloth and advances them one by one for the emperor.

sentences.zh: 欲射，協律郎舉麾，先奏鼓吹，及奏樂騶虞五節，御及射，第一矢與第六節相應，第二矢與第七節相應，以至九節。

translations.literal: When about to shoot, the pitch-regulator raises the baton; court music is played first, then the music Zouyu in five sections; for the emperor's shooting, the first arrow matches the sixth section, the second the seventh, up to the ninth.
translations.idiomatic: When about to shoot, the pitch-regulator raises the baton; court music is played first, then the music Zouyu in five sections; for the emperor's shooting, the first arrow matches the sixth section, the second the seventh, up to the ninth.

sentences.zh: 協律郎偃麾，樂止。

translations.literal: The pitch-regulator lowers the baton; music stops.
translations.idiomatic: The pitch-regulator lowers the baton; music stops.

sentences.zh: 千牛將軍以矢行奏，中曰「獲」，下曰「留」，上曰「揚」，左曰「左方」，右曰「右方」。

translations.literal: The Imperial Ox general reports by the arrow's course: hit says "Captured"; short says "Held"; over says "Raised"; left says "Left square"; right says "Right square."
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Ox general reports by the arrow's course: hit says "Captured"; short says "Held"; over says "Raised"; left says "Left square"; right says "Right square."

sentences.zh: 留，謂矢短不及侯；

translations.literal: "Held" means the arrow fell short of the target;
translations.idiomatic: "Held" means the arrow fell short of the target;

sentences.zh: 揚，謂矢過侯；

translations.literal: "Raised" means the arrow passed the target;
translations.idiomatic: "Raised" means the arrow passed the target;

sentences.zh: 左、右，謂矢偏不正。

translations.literal: left and right mean the arrow was deflected off true.
translations.idiomatic: left and right mean the arrow was deflected off center.

sentences.zh: 千牛將軍於御座東，西面受弓，退，付千牛於東階上。

translations.literal: The Imperial Ox general east of the imperial seat, facing west, receives the bow, withdraws, and gives it to the Imperial Ox on the east steps.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Ox general east of the imperial seat, facing west, receives the bow, withdraws, and gives it to the Imperial Ox on the east steps.

sentences.zh: 千牛郎將以笥受決、拾，奠於坫。

translations.literal: The Imperial Ox lieutenant receives thumb-ring and armguard in the quiver and places them on the altar.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Ox lieutenant receives thumb-ring and armguard in the quiver and places them on the altar.

sentences.zh: 侍射者進，升射席北面立，左旋，東面張弓，南面挾矢。

translations.literal: Attendant archers advance, ascend the shooting mat facing north, turn left, face east, draw the bow, and hold arrows to the south.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant archers advance, ascend the shooting mat facing north, turn left, face east, draw the bow, and hold arrows to the south.

sentences.zh: 協律郎舉麾，乃作樂，不作鼓吹。

translations.literal: The pitch-regulator raises the baton; music is performed without court music.
translations.idiomatic: The pitch-regulator raises the baton; music is performed without court music.

sentences.zh: 樂奏狸首三節，然後發矢。

translations.literal: The music Lishou is played in three sections; then arrows are loosed.
translations.idiomatic: The music Lishou is played in three sections; then arrows are loosed.

sentences.zh: 若侍射者多，則齊發。

translations.literal: If there are many attendant archers, they shoot together.
translations.idiomatic: If there are many attendant archers, they shoot together.

sentences.zh: 第一發與第四節相應，第二發與第五節相應，以至七節。

translations.literal: The first shot matches the fourth section, the second the fifth, up to the seventh section.
translations.idiomatic: The first shot matches the fourth section, the second the fifth, up to the seventh section.

sentences.zh: 協律郎偃麾，樂止。

translations.literal: The pitch-regulator lowers the baton; music stops.
translations.idiomatic: The pitch-regulator lowers the baton; music stops.

sentences.zh: 弓右旋，東西㢮弓，如面立，乃退復西階下，立。

translations.literal: The bow is turned right, east-west the bow is hung as when facing, then they withdraw to below the west steps and stand.
translations.idiomatic: The bow is turned right, east-west the bow is hung as when facing, then they withdraw to below the west steps and stand.

sentences.zh: 司馬升自西階，自西楹前，南面，揮弓，命取矢。

translations.literal: The Master of Horse ascends by the west steps, before the west pillar, faces south, waves the bow, and orders arrows collected.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Horse ascends by the west steps, before the west pillar, faces south, waves the bow, and orders arrows collected.

sentences.zh: 取矢者以御矢付千牛於東階下，侍射者釋弓於位，庭前北面東上。

translations.literal: Collectors give the imperial arrows to the Imperial Ox below the east steps; attendant archers release bows at their places, in the courtyard facing north with the east uppermost.
translations.idiomatic: Collectors give the imperial arrows to the Imperial Ox below the east steps; attendant archers release bows at their places, in the courtyard facing north with the east uppermost.

sentences.zh: 有司奏請賞罰，侍中稱：「制曰可。

translations.literal: The responsible office reports requesting rewards and penalties; the attendant within the palace says: "The command is: permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible office reports requesting rewards and penalties; the palace attendant says: "The command is: permitted.

sentences.zh: 」有司立楅之西，東面，監唱射矢。

translations.literal: " The responsible office stands west of the arrow-holders, faces east, and supervises announcing the shooting arrows.
translations.idiomatic: " The responsible office stands west of the arrow-holders, faces east, and supervises announcing the shooting arrows.

sentences.zh: 取矢者各唱中者姓名。

translations.literal: Collectors each announce the names of those who hit.
translations.idiomatic: Collectors each announce the names of those who hit.

sentences.zh: 中者立於東階下，西面北上；

translations.literal: Those who hit stand below the east steps, facing west with the north uppermost;
translations.idiomatic: Those who hit stand below the east steps, facing west with the north uppermost;

sentences.zh: 不中者立於西階下，東面北上。

translations.literal: those who miss stand below the west steps, facing east with the north uppermost.
translations.idiomatic: those who miss stand below the west steps, facing east with the north uppermost.

sentences.zh: 俱再拜。

translations.literal: All twice bow.
translations.idiomatic: All bow twice.

sentences.zh: 有司於東階下以付賞物。

translations.literal: The responsible office below the east steps gives out rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible office below the east steps gives out rewards.

sentences.zh: 酌者於罰尊西，東面，跪，奠爵於豐上。

translations.literal: Pourers west of the penalty vessel, facing east, kneel and place goblets on the mound.
translations.idiomatic: Pourers west of the penalty vessel, facing east, kneel and place goblets on the mound.

sentences.zh: 不中者進豐南，北面跪，取爵，立飲，卒爵，奠豐下。

translations.literal: Those who miss advance south of the mound, face north and kneel, take the goblet, stand and drink, finish the goblet, and place it below the mound.
translations.idiomatic: Those who miss advance south of the mound, face north and kneel, take the goblet, stand and drink, finish the goblet, and place it below the mound.

sentences.zh: 酌者北面跪，取虛爵酌奠，不中者以次繼飲，皆如初。

translations.literal: Pourers face north and kneel, take the empty goblet, pour and place it; those who miss continue drinking in order, all as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Pourers face north and kneel, take the empty goblet, pour and place it; those who miss continue drinking in order, all as at first.

sentences.zh: 典謁引王公以下及侍射者，皆庭前北面相對為首，再拜訖，引出。

translations.literal: The Director of Audience leads kings, dukes, and those below and the attendant archers; all in the courtyard face north in pairs as head, twice bow, then are led out.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Audience leads kings, dukes, and those below and the attendant archers; all in the courtyard face north in pairs as head, bow twice, then are led out.

sentences.zh: 持鈒隊復位。

translations.literal: Halberd-bearing companies return to their places.
translations.idiomatic: Halberd-bearing companies return to their places.

sentences.zh: 皇帝入，奏樂，警蹕。

translations.literal: The emperor enters; music plays; the guard of honor clears the way.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor enters; music plays; the guard of honor clears the way.

sentences.zh: 有司以弓矢出中門外，侍射者出。

translations.literal: The responsible office takes bows and arrows out the central gate; attendant archers go out.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible office takes bows and arrows out the central gate; attendant archers go out.

sentences.zh: 若特射無侍射之人，則不設楅，不陳賞罰。

translations.literal: If special archery without attendant archers, arrow-holders are not set and rewards and penalties are not displayed.
translations.idiomatic: If special archery without attendant archers, arrow-holders are not set and rewards and penalties are not displayed.

sentences.zh: 若燕遊小射，則常服，不陳樂縣，不行會禮。

translations.literal: If informal pleasure shooting, ordinary dress is worn, palace music is not displayed, and the assembly rite is not performed.
translations.idiomatic: If informal pleasure shooting, ordinary dress is worn, palace music is not displayed, and the assembly rite is not performed.

sentences.zh: 合朔伐鼓。

translations.literal: Beating drums at new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Beating drums at new moon.

sentences.zh: 其日前二刻，郊社令及門僕赤幘絳衣，守四門，令巡門監察。

translations.literal: Two quarters before that day, the directors of suburban and altar offices and gate servants wear crimson headcloths and crimson robes, guard the four gates, and patrol the gates.
translations.idiomatic: Two quarters before that day, the directors of suburban and altar offices and gate servants wear crimson headcloths and crimson robes, guard the four gates, and patrol the gates.

sentences.zh: 鼓吹令平巾幘、袴褶，帥工人以方色執麾旒，分置四門屋下，設龍蛇鼓於右。

translations.literal: The Director of Court Music in plain headcloth and trousers with jacket leads workers holding banners of the quarter's color at the four gate houses, with dragon-and-serpent drums to the right.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Court Music in plain headcloth and trousers with jacket leads workers holding banners of the quarter's color at the four gate houses, with dragon-and-serpent drums to the right.

sentences.zh: 東門者立於北塾，南面；

translations.literal: Those at the east gate stand in the north school, facing south;
translations.idiomatic: Those at the east gate stand in the north school, facing south;

sentences.zh: 南門者立於東塾，西面；

translations.literal: those at the south gate stand in the east school, facing west;
translations.idiomatic: those at the south gate stand in the east school, facing west;

sentences.zh: 西門者立於南塾，北面；

translations.literal: those at the west gate stand in the south school, facing north;
translations.idiomatic: those at the west gate stand in the south school, facing north;

sentences.zh: 北門者立於西塾，東面。

translations.literal: those at the north gate stand in the west school, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: those at the north gate stand in the west school, facing east.

sentences.zh: 隊正一人平巾幘、袴褶，執刀，帥衞士五人執五兵立於鼓外，矛在東，戟在南，斧、鉞在西，矟在北。

translations.literal: One squad leader in plain headcloth and trousers with jacket holds a sword and leads five guards holding the five weapons outside the drums—spear east, halberd south, axe and battle-axe west, long spear north.
translations.idiomatic: One squad leader in plain headcloth and trousers with jacket holds a sword and leads five guards holding the five weapons outside the drums—spear east, halberd south, axe and battle-axe west, long spear north.

sentences.zh: 郊社令立𥎞於社壇四隅，以朱絲繩縈之。

translations.literal: The director of suburban and altar offices sets drums at the four corners of the altar mound, bound with crimson silk cord.
translations.idiomatic: The director of suburban and altar offices sets drums at the four corners of the altar mound, bound with crimson silk cord.

sentences.zh: 太史一人赤幘、赤衣，立於社壇北，向日觀變。

translations.literal: One grand astrologer in crimson headcloth and crimson robe stands north of the altar mound, facing the sun to observe the change.
translations.idiomatic: One grand astrologer in crimson headcloth and crimson robe stands north of the altar mound, facing the sun to observe the change.

sentences.zh: 黃麾次之；

translations.literal: Yellow banners next;
translations.idiomatic: Yellow banners next;

sentences.zh: 龍鼓一次之，在北；

translations.literal: dragon drums once next, to the north;
translations.idiomatic: dragon drums once next, to the north;

sentences.zh: 弓一、矢四次之。

translations.literal: one bow, four times arrows next.
translations.idiomatic: one bow, four times arrows next.

sentences.zh: 諸兵鼓立候變。

translations.literal: All military drums stand waiting for the change.
translations.idiomatic: All military drums stand waiting for the change.

sentences.zh: 日有變，史官曰：「祥有變。

translations.literal: When the sun changes, the astrologer says: "An auspicious sign has changed.
translations.idiomatic: When the sun changes, the astrologer says: "An auspicious sign has changed.

sentences.zh: 」工人舉麾，龍鼓發聲如雷。

translations.literal: " Workers raise banners; dragon drums sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: " Workers raise banners; dragon drums sound like thunder.

sentences.zh: 史官曰：「止。

translations.literal: The astrologer says: "Stop.
translations.idiomatic: The astrologer says: "Stop.

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " They then stop.
translations.idiomatic: " They then stop.

sentences.zh: 其日，皇帝素服，避正殿，百官廢務，自府史以上皆素服，各於其廳事之前，重行，每等異位，向日立。

translations.literal: On that day the emperor wears plain dress, avoids the main hall, and all officials suspend duties; from prefectural clerks up all wear plain dress, each before his office, double ranks, each rank separate, facing the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On that day the emperor wears plain dress, avoids the main hall, and all officials suspend duties; from prefectural clerks up all wear plain dress, each before his office, double ranks, each rank separate, facing the sun.

sentences.zh: 明復而止。

translations.literal: When brightness returns, it ceases.
translations.idiomatic: When brightness returns, it ceases.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年八月，日有食之，有司將伐鼓，德宗不許。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Zhenyuan, there was an eclipse; the responsible office was about to beat drums; Emperor Dezong did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year of Zhenyuan, there was an eclipse; the responsible office was about to beat drums; Emperor Dezong did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 太常卿董晉言：「伐鼓所以責陰而助陽也，請聽有司依經伐鼓。

translations.literal: The Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple Dong Jin said: "Beating drums is to reproach yin and assist yang; I request that the responsible office be allowed to beat drums according to the classic.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple Dong Jin said: "Beating drums is to reproach yin and assist yang; I request that the responsible office be allowed to beat drums according to the classic.

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: " No reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: " No reply was given.

sentences.zh: 由是其禮遂廢。

translations.literal: From this the rite was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: From this the rite was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 大儺之禮。

translations.literal: The great nuo exorcism rite.
translations.idiomatic: The great nuo exorcism rite.

sentences.zh: 選人年十二以上、十六以下為侲子，假面，赤布袴褶。

translations.literal: Selectees aged twelve and above to sixteen below serve as nuo youths, masked, in crimson cloth trousers with jacket.
translations.idiomatic: Selectees aged twelve and above to sixteen below serve as nuo youths, masked, in crimson cloth trousers with jacket.

sentences.zh: 二十四人為一隊，六人為列。

translations.literal: Twenty-four form one company; six form a rank.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four form one company; six form a rank.

sentences.zh: 執事十二人，赤幘、赤衣，麻鞭。

translations.literal: Twelve attendants in crimson headcloths and crimson robes, with hemp whips.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve attendants in crimson headcloths and crimson robes, with hemp whips.

sentences.zh: 工人二十二人，其一人方相氏，假面，黃金四目，蒙熊皮，黑衣、朱裳，右執楯；

translations.literal: Twenty-two workers; one is the exorcist chief Fangxiang, masked, gold four eyes, covered in bear skin, black robe and crimson skirt, right hand holding shield;
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-two workers; one is the exorcist chief Fangxiang, masked, gold four eyes, covered in bear skin, black robe and crimson skirt, right hand holding shield;

sentences.zh: 其一人為唱帥，假面，皮衣，執棒；

translations.literal: one is the chant leader, masked, leather coat, holding a staff;
translations.idiomatic: one is the chant leader, masked, leather coat, holding a staff;

sentences.zh: 鼓、角各十，合為一隊。

translations.literal: ten drums and ten horns each, forming one company.
translations.idiomatic: ten drums and ten horns each, forming one company.

sentences.zh: 隊別鼓吹令一人，太卜令一人，各監所部；

translations.literal: Each company has one Director of Court Music and one Director of Divination, each supervising his section;
translations.idiomatic: Each company has one Director of Court Music and one Director of Divination, each supervising his section;

sentences.zh: 巫師二人。

translations.literal: two shamans.
translations.idiomatic: two shamans.

sentences.zh: 以逐惡鬼于禁中。

translations.literal: To drive evil ghosts from within the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: To drive evil ghosts from within the forbidden precinct.

sentences.zh: 有司預備每門雄鷄及酒，擬於宮城正門、皇城諸門磔攘，設祭。

translations.literal: The responsible office prepares a cock and wine at each gate, intending dismemberment and expulsion at the palace city main gate and imperial city gates, and sets offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible office prepares a cock and wine at each gate, intending dismemberment and expulsion at the palace city main gate and imperial city gates, and sets offerings.

sentences.zh: 太祝一人，齋郎三人，右校為瘞埳，各於皇城中門外之右。

translations.literal: One Grand Invoker, three abstinence attendants; the Right Works Office makes burial pits, each to the right outside the imperial city central gate.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Invoker, three abstinence attendants; the Right Works Office makes burial pits, each to the right outside the imperial city central gate.

sentences.zh: 前一日之夕，儺者赴集所，具其器服以待事。

translations.literal: On the evening of the day before, exorcists assemble at the gathering place and prepare implements and dress to await the affair.
translations.idiomatic: On the evening of the day before, exorcists assemble at the gathering place and prepare implements and dress to await the affair.

sentences.zh: 其日未明，諸衞依時刻勒所部，屯門列仗，近仗入陳於階。

translations.literal: Before dawn that day, each guard assembles its section by the hour, arrays guards at the gates, and close attendants enter and are arrayed on the steps.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn that day, each guard assembles its section by the hour, arrays guards at the gates, and close attendants enter and are arrayed on the steps.

sentences.zh: 鼓吹令帥儺者各集於宮門外。

translations.literal: The Director of Court Music leads exorcists to assemble outside each palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Court Music leads exorcists to assemble outside each palace gate.

sentences.zh: 內侍詣皇帝所御殿前奏「侲子備，請逐疫」。

translations.literal: A palace eunuch goes before the hall where the emperor will preside and reports: "The nuo youths are ready; I request to drive out the pestilence."
translations.idiomatic: A palace eunuch goes before the hall where the emperor will preside and reports: "The nuo youths are ready; I request to drive out the pestilence."

sentences.zh: 出命寺伯六人，分引儺者於長樂門、永安門以入，至左右上閤，鼓譟以進。

translations.literal: He orders six temple stewards to lead exorcists in separately through the Changle Gate and Yongan Gate to the left and right upper pavilions, beating drums and clamoring as they advance.
translations.idiomatic: He orders six temple stewards to lead exorcists in separately through the Changle Gate and Yongan Gate to the left and right upper pavilions, beating drums and clamoring as they advance.

sentences.zh: 方相氏執戈揚楯唱，侲子和，曰：「甲作食𣧑，胇胃食虎，雄伯食魅，騰簡食不祥，攬諸食咎，伯奇食夢，彊梁、祖明共食磔死寄生，委隨食觀，錯斷食巨，窮奇、騰根共食蠱，凡使一十二神追惡凶，赫汝軀，拉汝幹，節解汝肉，抽汝肺腸，汝不急去，後者為糧。

translations.literal: Fangxiang holds spear and raises shield chanting; nuo youths respond, saying: "Jia-zuo eats 𣧑, Fei-wei eats tigers, Xiong-bo eats demons, Teng-jian eats ill omens, Lan-zhu eats calamities, Bo-qi eats dreams, Qiang-liang and Zu-ming together eat dismembered dead parasites, Wei-sui eats Guan, Cuo-duan eats Ju, Qiong-qi and Teng-gen together eat gu poison—twelve spirits in all pursue evil and misfortune: blaze your bodies, tear your sinews, joint by joint strip your flesh, draw out lungs and guts—if you do not flee swiftly, those behind will be your food.
translations.idiomatic: Fangxiang holds spear and raises shield chanting; nuo youths respond, saying: "Jia-zuo eats 𣧑, Fei-wei eats tigers, Xiong-bo eats demons, Teng-jian eats ill omens, Lan-zhu eats calamities, Bo-qi eats dreams, Qiang-liang and Zu-ming together eat dismembered dead parasites, Wei-sui eats Guan, Cuo-duan eats Ju, Qiong-qi and Teng-gen together eat gu poison—twelve spirits in all pursue evil and misfortune: blaze your bodies, tear your sinews, joint by joint strip your flesh, draw out lungs and guts—if you do not flee swiftly, those behind will be your food.

sentences.zh: 」周呼訖，前後鼓譟而出，諸隊各趨順天門以出，分詣諸城門，出郭而止。

translations.literal: " When the round chant ends, they drum and clamor out front and rear; each company hurries to the Gate of Obeying Heaven to go out, proceeds separately to each city gate, and stops outside the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: " When the round chant ends, they drum and clamor out front and rear; each company hurries to the Gate of Obeying Heaven to go out, proceeds separately to each city gate, and stops outside the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 儺者將出，祝布神席，當中門南向。

translations.literal: When the exorcists are about to go out, the invoker spreads the spirit mat facing south at the central gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the exorcists are about to go out, the invoker spreads the spirit mat facing south at the central gate.

sentences.zh: 出訖，宰手、齋郎疈牲匈磔之神席之西，藉以席，北首。

translations.literal: When they have gone out, the chief butcher and abstinence attendants dismember the victim's chest and dismember it west of the spirit mat, spread a mat, head to the north.
translations.idiomatic: When they have gone out, the chief butcher and abstinence attendants dismember the victim's chest and dismember it west of the spirit mat, spread a mat, head to the north.

sentences.zh: 齋郎酌清酒，太祝受，奠之。

translations.literal: Abstinence attendants pour clear wine; the Grand Invoker receives it and places it.
translations.idiomatic: Abstinence attendants pour clear wine; the Grand Invoker receives it and places it.

sentences.zh: 祝史持版於座右，跪讀祝文曰：「維某年歲次月朔日，天子遣太祝臣姓名昭告于太陰之神。

translations.literal: The invoker-clerk holds the placard at the mat's right side, kneels and reads the prayer: "In such-and-such a year, on such-and-such a day of the first month, the Son of Heaven dispatches Grand Invoker, your subject so-and-so, to announce to the spirit of the Great Yin.
translations.idiomatic: The invoker-clerk holds the placard at the mat's right side, kneels and reads the prayer: "In such-and-such a year, on such-and-such a day of the first month, the Son of Heaven dispatches Grand Invoker, your subject so-and-so, to announce to the spirit of the Great Yin.

sentences.zh: 」興，奠版于席，乃舉牲幷酒瘞於埳。

translations.literal: " He rises, places the placard on the mat, then lifts the victim and wine together and buries them in the pit.
translations.idiomatic: " He rises, places the placard on the mat, then lifts the victim and wine together and buries them in the pit.
